input_signals.name: Rollover-Funded Acquisition Tilt
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(dlc, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(gdwl, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Rising short-term debt is especially negative when it finances a shift toward acquired intangibles and goodwill rather than organic R&D.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the broad external-financing anomaly with a narrower rollover-financing channel and removes the degenerate 0/1 conditioning structure. The continuous goodwill-minus-R&D change tests whether fragile financing is supporting acquisition accounting rather than internal innovation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( gdwl, at ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Stable R&D
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(lt, at), 1))), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), RANK(VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent, stable R&D undertaken while liability dependence is falling is more likely internally funded productive innovation than externally financed experimentation.
input_signals.reasoning: This refines the prior liability-light R&D result by distinguishing durable R&D programs from volatile spending spikes. Falling liabilities reduce the concern that R&D is being sustained by fragile financing, while low R&D volatility suggests a committed innovation pipeline.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( growth( ratio( lt, at ), 1 ) ) ), sub( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), rank( vol( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Retired R&D Continuity
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(dltr, at)), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that retire debt while sustaining an upward R&D intensity trend are more likely funding innovation from operating strength rather than external capital-market dependence.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts the debt-retrenchment idea from sparse advertising to better-covered R&D and focuses on financing discipline rather than payout behavior. A high signal requires both net debt reduction and continuing organic innovation commitment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sub( rank( ratio( dltr, at ) ), rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Acquisition Debt Cleanup
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(dltr, at), RATIO(dltis, at))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that reduce debt while goodwill intensity falls are more likely digesting prior acquisitions successfully rather than carrying externally financed acquisition overhang.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the unidentified all-positive goodwill-realization product by focusing on post-acquisition balance-sheet repair. A high score requires both net debt retirement and declining goodwill exposure, consistent with integration discipline or reduced overpayment risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ratio( dltr, at ), ratio( dltis, at ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Prior-Goodwill Debt Cleanup
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(dltr, at), RATIO(dltis, at))), MUL(LAG(TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 5), 1), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt retirement is most informative after a firm has recently carried high goodwill and is now reducing goodwill intensity, consistent with disciplined post-acquisition cleanup.
input_signals.reasoning: The lagged own-history goodwill rank identifies firms actually coming out of an acquisition-heavy state, rather than treating all goodwill declines alike. The financing leg requires net debt reduction, so the signal captures balance-sheet repair of prior intangible acquisition risk rather than a standalone goodwill change.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ratio( dltr, at ), ratio( dltis, at ) ) ), mul( lag( ts_rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 5 ), 1 ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )
